previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for diffuse back pain radiating to the flanks and neck, accompanied by weight loss and diarrhea. Initial CT showed pancolitis, and stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, and E. coli 0157. Flexible sigmoidoscopy revealed apthous ulcers, and biopsies confirmed chronic focally active colitis consistent with a Crohn’s flare. She was treated with IV ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, IV magnesium for hypomagnesemia, and supportive care. Her pain resolved, she advanced to a full diet, and her condition stabilized. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, mesalamine, and adjusted chronic medications, with follow-up arranged with gastroenterology and outpatient physical therapy.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with headache and left-sided weakness for
several hours.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:  There is no intracranial hemorrhage, edema, shift of normally
midline structures or evidence of acute major vascular territorial infarct. 
Old lacunar infarcts in the periventricular white matter are again noted. 
Ventricles and sulci are normal in size and configuration.  The gray-white
matter differentiation is preserved.  Other cisterns are symmetric.  Mastoid
air cells and paranasal sinuses are well aerated.

IMPRESSIONS:

1.  No acute infarct or intracranial hemorrhage.  MRI is more sensitive for
the detection of acute ischemia.

2.  Old periventricular lacunar infarcts.

EXAM:  MRI brain, MRA head, MRA neck.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease,
hypertension, back pain with left-sided headache, weakness, found to have
acute on chronic renal failure, rule out stroke.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and FLAIR, T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial
images of the brain were acquired.  3D time-of-flight MRA of the circle of
___ obtained.  2D and 3D time-of-flight MRA of the neck vessels acquired.

FINDINGS:  BRAIN MRI:

There is no acute infarct seen.  Mild changes of small vessel disease
identified with a chronic lacune in the left periventricular white matter.
There is no midline shift, mass effect, or hydrocephalus.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute infarct.  Mild-to-moderate chronic small
vessel disease changes.

MRA OF THE HEAD:

The head MRA demonstrates normal flow signal in the arteries of anterior and
posterior circulation.

IMPRESSION:  Normal MRA of the head.

MRA OF THE NECK:

2D and 3D time-of-flight MRA of the neck vessels demonstrates no evidence of
vascular occlusion or high-grade stenosis.  The examination is limited by
motion.

IMPRESSION:  Motion limited study demonstrate no vascular occlusion or high-
grade stenosis.

CHEST

HISTORY:  Hypertension, renal disease, back pain, fever, rule out pneumonia.

One view.  Comparison with ___.  The lungs remain clear except for minimal
streaky density at the left base consistent with subsegmental atelectasis or
scarring.  The heart and mediastinal structures are unchanged.  The bony
thorax is grossly intact.

IMPRESSION:  No active pulmonary disease.

HISTORY:  Diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic renal failure, right and
left arm weakness.  Right arm three views.  Left arm three views.

RIGHT SHOULDER:  There are moderate to moderately severe degenerative changes
about the AC joint, and ill-definition in the cortex along distal clavicle
consistent with resorptive changes related to rheumatoid arthritis. Mild-to-
moderate degenerative spurring is present about the glenohumeral joint.  There
is spurring along the undersurface of the acromion.  No glenohumeral erosions
are identified.  Probable diffuse osteopenia.  No hydroxyapatite is detected
about the shoulder joint.  Right shoulder x-ray examination otherwise within
normal limits.

LEFT SHOULDER:  There are moderate to moderately severe degenerative changes
about the AC joint, with marginal spurring. There are also marginal spurs
about the glenohumeral joint.  Probable diffuse osteopenia.  Question tiny
focus of calcification in soft tissues adjacent to greater tuberosity.
Otherwise, left shoulder x-ray examination within normal limits.  No erosions
identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Probable diffuse osteopenia.

2.  Degenerative changes about both AC joints and to lesser extent both
glenohumeral joints.  Mild resorption changes of distal right clavicle may be
secondary to RA. No other erosions identified. 

3.  Minimal calcification adjacent to left rotator cuff tendon could represent
a small focus of hydroxyapatite (calcific tendonitis).
